title: In situ detection of protein-protein interaction by proximity ligation assay in patient derived brain tumor stem cells
protocol: Maintain patient derived BTSCs in 5% CO2 at 37°C in BTSC growth medium and in T-75 culture flasks for cells in suspension as spheres.
Collect BTSC spheres by gently mixing the flask to ensure collection of as many spheres as possible, and transfer the content to a 15 mL falcon tube using a 10 mL pipette.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 200 × g at room temperature (22°C–25°C).
Carefully aspirate media with a vacuum pump as not to disturb the pellet.
Add 200 μL Accumax cell dissociation solution to the pellet.
Gently triturate the sample using a P200 pipette.
Incubate at 37°C for a total of 10 min, gently flicking the tube 3-5 times after 5 minutes.
Following the incubation period, add 800 μL of BTSC growth media.
Triturate the cell suspension using a 1000 μL pipette followed by a 200 μL pipette to complete dissociation if required.
Count the number of viable cells using an exclusion dye such as trypan blue.
Centrifuge cells following Accumax dissociation to discard media.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL of BTSC growth media containing 10% DMSO.
Transfer resuspended cells to a cryogenic tube and store at -80°C overnight (12-16 hours).
Transfer cryopreserved cells to a liquid nitrogen storage box for long-term storage.
Seed cells at a density of ∼0.5 × 10^6 cells in a T-75 flask with 10 mL BTSC growth medium.
Add 3 mL of fresh BTSC media to the flask if spheres are less than 150 μm and media is acidic.
Warm BTSC plating medium in a water bath at 37°C for ∼10 min.
Incubate wells with 300 μl of warm BTSC plating media in a biological safety cabinet.
Collect media and cells by gently mixing and pipetting all the BTSC spheres using a 10 ml serological pipette.
Transfer collected media and cells to a 15 ml polypropylene conical tube.
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 200 × g at room temperature (22°C–25°C).
Discard the media by aspiration.
Add 200 μL of Accumax solution and mix gently using a P200 micropipette.
Incubate at 37°C for 10 minutes in the incubator or in a water bath.
Gently flick the tubes 3–5 times after 5 minutes to prevent spheres from settling down.
Remove the cell-Accumax containing tubes from the incubator and tritrate gently 10 times using a P200 micropipette with low retention filtered long pipette tips to homogenize.
Add 800 μL of BTSC plating media to the 200 μL Accumax-cell suspension.
Maintain BTSCs in serum-free medium.
Count the number of viable cells using trypan blue.
Prepare a cell suspension of 10^5 cells/mL in BTSC plating medium.
Homogenize the cell suspension by pipetting up and down with a P1000 micropipette set at 800 μL.
Remove the media from the wells from step 13.
Plate BTSCs at a density of ∼28 × 10^3 cells/cm² by distributing 200 μL of cell suspension to each 0.7 cm² well.
Incubate the newly plated cells under the biological hood for 5 min with minimum vibrations.
Incubate cells for 1 h at 37°C with 5% CO₂ in an incubator.
Ensure that BTSC spheres are well dissociated with no apparent cell aggregates.
Check wells before incubating at 37°C to ensure homogeneous cell distribution.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 1 hour without shaking until cells adhere.
Verify under microscope after 1 hour of incubation to confirm cell adherence and uniformity.
Aspirate media from each chamber.
Wash cells by distributing 200 μL 1× PBS to each chamber gently.
Remove PBS immediately and repeat wash once more with 200 μL 1× PBS.
Fix the cells by adding 100 μL of room temperature (22°C–25°C) 4% PFA in 1× PBS to each well.
Incubate cells for 15 min at room temperature (22°C–25°C).
Aspirate PFA.
Wash the cells twice with room temperature (22°C–25°C) 1× PBS.
Store fixed cells at 4°C for later processing if needed.
If storing fixed cells for less than 1 week, fill the well with 1× PBS and wrap it with parafilm to prevent drying.
For storage of fixed cells longer than 1 week, store sample at 4°C in 1× PBS containing 0.01% sodium azide.
Remove the PBS solution with a vacuum pump.
Add 100 μL of permeabilization solution (0.5% Triton X in 1× PBS).
Incubate at room temperature (22°C–25°C) for 20 min.
Remove the permeabilization solution with a vacuum pump.
Wash twice with room temperature (22°C–25°C) 1× PBS.
Mix the blocking solution and add 100 μL of the blocking solution to each well.
Incubate the chamber slides in a heated humid chamber for 1 h at 37°C under gentle agitation on a up/down rocking shaker (2 rpm).
Dilute primary antibodies to the optimal dilution in antibody diluent buffer.
Use mouse galectin-1 and rabbit HOXA5 antibodies at a 1:400 dilution in the diluent buffer.
Prepare knockout cells for the protein of interest as negative controls.
Probe LGALS1 CRISPR KO BTSCs with galectin-1 and HOXA5 primary antibodies for negative control 1.
Probe HOXA5 CRISPR KO BTSCs with galectin-1 and HOXA5 primary antibodies for negative control 2.
Use a combination of primary antibody and anti-IgG as an alternative negative control.
Combine mouse anti-galectin-1 and rabbit anti-IgG for a negative control.
Combine rabbit anti-HOXA5 and mouse anti-IgG for another negative control.
Add 100 μL of 1× PBS to each well without removing the blocking solution.
Aspirate the mixture using a vacuum pump.
Alternatively, use a micropipette for aspiration if working with fewer samples.
Add 40 μL of primary antibody-diluent solution to each well.
Incubate overnight (12–16 h) at 4°C in a humid chamber on an up/down rocking shaker.
Fill unused wells with 1× PBS.
Remove buffer A from the fridge and bring it to room temperature (∼1 h).
Add 300 μL of wash buffer A to each well without removing the primary antibody-diluent solution.
Aspirate using a vacuum pump.
Add 300 μL of wash buffer A to each well.
Incubate the wells for 5 min at room temperature (22°C–25°C) on an up/down rocking shaker at low speed (2 rpm).
Aspirate the wash buffer A from each well.
Repeat washing twice with wash buffer A.
While washing, take PLA Plus and Minus probes out of the fridge (4°C) and vortex briefly.
Dilute 5× PLA probes in antibody diluent buffer at a 1:5 ratio.
Prepare 40 μL of 1× PLA probe mix for each sample, including negative controls.
Aspirate wash buffer A from last washing using a vacuum pump.
Add 40 μL of 1× PLA probe mix to each sample and negative controls.
Incubate the samples in a preheated humid chamber at 37°C on an up/down rocking shaker at low speed (2 rpm) for 1 hour.
Without removing the PLA probe, add 300 μL of wash buffer A to each well.
Rapidly aspirate using a vacuum pump.
Add 300 μL of wash buffer A to each well and incubate for 5 min at room temperature (22°C–25°C) in a humid chamber on an up/down rocking shaker at low speed (2 rpm).
Aspirate the wash buffer A.
Repeat washing twice.
During the washing step, prepare the ligation solution for the next step.
Thaw the 5× ligation buffer stored at −20°C before use.
Prepare 1× ligation buffer by diluting the 5× ligation buffer in Milli-Q water.
For each sample, prepare 40 μL of 1× ligation buffer.
Ensure the ligation buffer is completely thawed and well homogenized prior to use.
Keep prepared 1× ligation buffer at room temperature.
Retrieve ligase (1 U/μL) from the freezer using a freezer block (-20°C).
Prepare 40 μL of 1× ligase solution per reaction immediately before addition to the sample.
Add ligase to the 1× ligation buffer immediately prior to adding it to the sample.
Keep ligase mix on the freezer block.
Mix well for multiple samples and negative controls before applying them to the wells.
Gently remove wash buffer A from the last wash using a vacuum pump.
Add 40 μL of ligation reaction mixture into each well including negative controls.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min at 37°C in a humid chamber under gentle agitation on an up/down rocking shaker (2 rpm).
Without removing the ligation-ligase solution, add 300 μL of wash buffer A to each well and rapidly aspirate using a vacuum pump.
Incubate with 300 μL of wash buffer A for 5 min at room temperature in a humid chamber on an up/down rocking shaker at low speed (2 rpm).
Aspirate wash buffer A and repeat the washing process twice.
Thaw the 5× amplification buffer stored at -20°C.
Mix the amplification buffer to ensure complete thawing and thorough mixing.
Prepare 40 μL of amplification buffer per reaction.
Retrieve the polymerase enzyme (10 U/μL) from the freezer using a freeze block (-20°C).
Prepare 40 μL of polymerase solution per reaction.
Add the polymerase to the 1× amplification buffer immediately prior to addition to the sample.
Keep the prepared mix at room temperature (22°C–25°C) protected from light while adding polymerase to the buffer.
Prepare a master mixture for multiple samples and negative controls, mixing well before use.
Gently remove wash buffer A using a vacuum pump after the last wash.
Add 40 μL of amplification mix into each well, including negative controls.
Incubate at 37°C for 100 minutes in a humid chamber under gentle agitation (2 rpm).
Bring wash buffer B to room temperature before use.
Without removing amplification-polymerase solution, add 300 μL of wash buffer B to each well.
Rapidly aspirate using a vacuum pump after adding wash buffer B.
Add 300 μL of wash buffer B to each well.
Incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature (22°C–25°C) on a humid chamber with an up/down rocking shaker at low speed (2 rpm).
Aspirate the wash buffer B.
Repeat washing with another 10-minute incubation of 300 μL of wash buffer B.
Aspirate the wash buffer B after the second incubation.
Wash with 300 μL of the 0.01× wash buffer B for 1 minute.
Aspirate the 0.01× wash buffer B using a vacuum pump.
Separate the chamber from the slide using the removal tool.
Remove any remaining liquid on the slide by holding it horizontally on filter paper or a paper towel.
Air-dry the slide for 3 minutes at room temperature (22°C–25°C) and protect from light.
Add 3 μL of mounting medium with DAPI on each sample slide section.
Place a rectangular cover glass on the slide to ensure even spreading of the mounting medium over the samples.
Avoid forming air bubbles under the coverslip during this process.
Seal the edges of the coverslip to the slide with clear nail polish.
Keep the slides under the fume hood for 30 minutes and protected from light to allow the nail polish sealing to dry.
Visualize PLA signal using a fluorescence microscope with appropriate filters for DAPI and the used fluorophore.
Use a 63× oil objective lens on a laser scanning confocal microscope (ZEISS LSM 800) to capture images.
Maintain identical acquisition parameters for experimental and control conditions.
Capture images of control BTSCs, LGALS1 CRISPR KO, and HOXA5 CRISPR KO BTSCs subjected to PLA.
Each red spot in the image represents a single interaction between HOXA5 and galectin1 molecules.
Include controls with primary antibody omission.
Perform PLA in LGALS1 CRISPR KO cells for control purposes.
Carry out PLA in HOXA5 CRISPR KO cells as another control measure.
Count the number of PLA dots and nuclei in each image.
Divide the number of PLA dots by the number of nuclei in each image to obtain the number of PLA dots per nucleus.
Perform statistical analysis using a student t-test to determine significance between the mean values of two compared conditions.
